title: Kian's Colorful Weather Tower
markdown:
The brilliant sun burst through Kian’s window, painting gold stripes across his floor. Birds burst into song, a happy chattering chorus. Kian stretched. Big stretch! It tickled his toes. Today felt special. He could practically taste the salty spray and feel the boat rocking.

He padded to his boat workshop. A little frown. Disaster. His weather wall! A rainbow exploded, then got stuck. Red for windy days. Blue for rain. Yellow for sunshine. Green for cloudy. They tumbled and jumbled. A gust had blown them around.

“Oh, fiddlesticks.” He tried to grab a sunny yellow note from last Tuesday. Buried under a heap of blue rain notes. “How will I pick the perfect day for Uncle Hari’s birthday boat trip? We need sunshine. This mess is just… a mess.”

Quack! Quack! Dottie the duck waddled in, bright eyes blinking, fluffy feathers shaking dewdrops. “Good morning, Kian! Tangled with a kite string? Your face is all scrunched up like a prune!”

Kian ran a hand through messy hair. “This weather wall. A jumbled disaster. I need last week’s sun and rain. Uncle Hari will be disappointed if we pick the wrong day.”

Dottie tilted her head, scanned the chaos, and pecked a bright red note on the floor. “Like counting my ducklings when they splash and dive. One minute five, the next, gone. I learned a trick. Line them up. Neat row. Super fast counting.” She nudged smooth grey pebbles. “One, two, three… all on this stone. Easy!”

Line them up. Brilliant. But how to line up paper notes stuck to the wall? Peeling them would be clutter, and the workshop already had boat parts and tools. Then Kian’s eyes sparkled, bright as the sunbeam.

“Pebbles for counting… lining up… Dottie, you’re a genius duck!”

He dashed to a dusty shelf and pulled down a sturdy wooden crate. Colourful building blocks, leftover from Uncle Hari’s boat-model project. Red. Blue. Yellow. Green. Just like the weather notes.

“What if we use blocks instead of notes? Stack them. Sunny day: yellow. Rainy: blue. Higher for more sun or rain. A picture of the week!”

Dottie quacked, wiggling. “A colourful tower of sunshine and puddles!”

Busy hands. Busy beak. They peeled sticky notes onto cardboard. Uncle Hari ambled in, face creased with a smile. “What’s this bustling? A mini-gale?” His laugh rumbled.

“A weather chart, Uncle Hari.” Kian held a bright yellow block. “Sunny day. Stack them.” Another yellow. “Two sunny days. More sunshine than one.”

Together they looked at old notes, day by day. Monday: cloudy — a sturdy green block. Tuesday: gusty — a tall proud red. Wednesday: super sunny — three yellow blocks, a cheerful tower. Thursday: a bit drippy — a small blue, a tiny puddle. Friday: bright and clear — tall yellow reaching. Saturday: quick shower. Sunday: breezy. Each block placed carefully. Colours made a lively pattern.

A magnificent chart stood on the workbench. Blocks rose to different heights. A clear picture. Tall yellow stacks: plenty of sunshine. Short blue and red: days for staying inside.

Uncle Hari patted Kian’s back. “Clear as a calm sea. A bar chart. It compares things. How much rain or sunshine. Helps us pick the very best day for a birthday sail.” He winked. “Saturday looks like a winner.”

Kian beamed. Organised blocks. Easy at a glance. “We can go on your birthday sail next Saturday. Perfectly sunny.”

Dottie bobbed. “Hooray for sunshine and birthday sails! Quack-tastic!”

Kian wondered what else might stand in towers — boats fixed, blueberries found, sea stories told — and clapped, grin as bright as morning. The yellow stack did not wobble. The boat, soon, would not either.
characters: Kian (a boat fixer), Dottie (a duck), Hari (an uncle)
author: StoryGen Community
